description: Shared Renovate preset for PRDCTR Foundation repositories. Extend it with { "extends": ["local>PRDCTR-Foundation/prdctr-common"] }.

It exists because nothing kept dependencies current: the shared packages were found two releases behind in one consumer, and the hand-maintained CVE override lists drifted behind the advisories they existed to satisfy, until the pre-commit audit gate refused every commit in three repos.

chore(deps) is the commit shape these repos' pr-title workflow accepts - chore is an allowed type everywhere and deps an allowed scope - because Renovate's own PRs must pass the same gate as anyone else's.
minimumReleaseAge mirrors the supply-chain cooldown already set in this repo's pnpm-workspace.yaml (1440 minutes), so a package compromised at publish time is not adopted the same day.
Nothing automerges and nothing ignores tests. A leftover config in one repo did both, which would have landed dependency bumps in a repo that had no CI at all until recently.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A vulnerability is the one case that should not wait for Monday, and should not sit out the cooldown either - the fix is the point.

packageRules.description: The shared packages are ours: no cooldown, and one PR rather than eighteen. Consumers drifting behind these is the drift that actually costs time.
Chain libraries move fast and break things. They get their own PR so a failure is attributable rather than buried in a batch.
Subsquid ships its stack as a set; splitting it produces PRs that cannot pass on their own.
Tooling is low risk and high noise, so it batches.
A major of anything gets read by a person, on its own.
